title: Ankhhaf, vizier and director of works under Khufu
summary: Ankhhaf was an ancient Egyptian prince, vizier, and director of royal works during the Fourth Dynasty (reigns of Khufu and Khafre, c. 26th century BCE). Identified as Khufu's half-brother, he managed the harbour basin at Ro-She Khufu during the construction of the Great Pyramid, as recorded in the contemporary Wadi al-Jarf papyri of Inspector Merer. His mastaba tomb at Giza (G 7510) yielded a celebrated painted limestone portrait bust now preserved at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

uncertainty.note: Active in the 4th Dynasty, specifically documented in Year 26 of Khufu (c. 2565 BCE) and under Khafre (c. 2520–2494 BCE per MFA Boston).
